title: Add runbook + triage links to meter drift alerts
author: Aisha Bello
body:
## Summary
This PR wires meter drift + data freshness alerts to the relevant Confluence runbooks and adds contextual links (Grafana panels + Snowflake queries) directly into alert annotations so on-call can self-serve triage without hunting through docs.

This is intentionally small/low-risk: no threshold changes and no alert routing changes. It only enriches annotations.

## Context
We’ve seen drift alerts trigger during month-end preview / late-arriving usage event windows. The alert itself tells you *what* drifted, but not *where to go next* (dashboard, query, or reconciliation playbook), which slows down response and increases Finance churn.

Related:
- ENG-4421 (meter drift alerts)
- PM-1872 (metering change control / runbook expectations)

## What changed
- Added `runbook_url` annotation to metering drift and freshness alerts.
- Added `dashboard_url` annotation pointing to the metering sanity Grafana dashboard pre-filtered to the alert labels (env/region/model/account when present).
- Added `triage_query` / `triage_query_url` annotations for the common drilldown query (by day/account/model/region) used to validate whether drift is due to duplicates, late events, or ledger lag.
- Added a small helper for URL construction to avoid hardcoding environment-specific Grafana base URLs.
- Added a short doc block in the alert rules file describing required labels and what to do if a Confluence page moves.

## Runbooks linked
- Meter drift triage runbook (on-call): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Meter+Drift+Alert+Triage
- Metering-to-invoice reconciliation playbook (Finance/RevRec): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/FIN/Metering-to-Invoice+Reconciliation+Playbook
- Meter sanity dashboard spec (owners, expected panels): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Meter+Sanity+Dashboard+Spec

Note: Confluence permissions apply; the runbook page includes a public-to-Engineering summary section and links out to restricted Finance-only content where required.

## Example (before/after)
Before:
- Alert: `meter_drift_vs_ledger` fired
- Message: “drift > 1% for account X in us-east-1”
- Next steps were tribal knowledge

After:
- Alert includes:
  - `Runbook`: Meter Drift Alert Triage
  - `Dashboard`: Metering Sanity → Drift panel (pre-filtered)
  - `Query`: Snowflake drilldown query (copy/paste + optional Snowsight link)

## Implementation notes
- Alert rule changes are under `observability/alerts/metering/*.yaml`.
- URL bases are read from existing `GRAFANA_BASE_URL` and `CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL` config (falls back to prod defaults in non-prod).
- The Snowflake query is provided as a multi-line annotation and also as a Snowsight link template. The query itself is parameterized using alert labels where present; if labels are missing we fall back to a generic query with TODO placeholders.
- No alert name changes to preserve paging history and silence matching.

## Testing
- Verified rule file parses with `promtool check rules`.
- Verified Alertmanager renders annotations correctly (local dev AM + staging ruleset).
- Clicked through generated Grafana links from a staging firing alert to confirm filters populate correctly.

## Rollout
- Merge to main, then ruleset deploy via `observability-pack` sync job (next 30-min window).
- No shadow-billing dependencies.

## Screenshots
(Internal) Added to PR comments: Alertmanager UI showing new annotations + Grafana deep link.

## Checklist
- [x] No paging behavior changes
- [x] Links work in staging
- [x] Runbook reviewed by Telemetry + Finance data owners

Co-authored-by: Mei Lin <mei.lin@redwoodinference.com>
commits: observability: add runbook_url/dashboard_url annotations to metering alerts
observability: add triage Snowflake query annotations and Snowsight link template
config: add helpers for environment-specific base URLs
docs: add maintenance notes for alert annotation links
review_conversation: Mei Lin (review): Can we ensure the Snowflake query annotation doesn’t leak restricted table names for folks without FIN access? The alert will page SRE who might not have ledger access.

Aisha Bello (author): Good call. Updated the query to reference the public reconciliation export view (billing_recon_export_v1) rather than the raw ledger tables, and added a note in the runbook for requesting access if deeper comparison is needed.

Logan Wright (review): Please avoid hardcoding the Confluence base URL. We’ve had to move pages / change domains before. Also, can we keep the runbook URL in one place so other alert rules can reuse it?

Aisha Bello (author): Addressed. Added CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL + a central constants file for metering runbook links. Alert rules now reference the shared helper. Also added a short maintenance section in README on updating links when pages move.
Caleb Johnson (review): The Grafana link template is using account_id label; some alerts only have account_slug. Can we support both? Also, ensure urlencoding.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated link builder to prefer account_id when present, else account_slug. Added urlencoding for all label values and a unit test for special characters.
Connor O'Brien (review): Any chance this changes alert fingerprints and breaks existing silences?
Aisha Bello (author): Annotations do not affect fingerprinting; only labels do. Confirmed we did not add/modify labels. Existing silences should continue to match.

Allison Grant (review): Can we add a short ‘first 5 minutes’ section to the runbook that clarifies expected drift during freeze windows / late events? Not required for this PR, but would reduce noise.

Aisha Bello (author): Added a minimal section to the runbook page (linked) noting freeze window expectations and pointing to the month-end close checklist. Kept PR code changes scoped to annotations only.
Mei Lin (approval): Approved once the query references the recon export view and the runbook clarifies access boundaries.
release_notes: - Metering drift/freshness alerts now include runbook + dashboard + query annotations to speed on-call triage (no behavioral changes to alerting).
